children: Texas Community Bancshares’ net interest income rose 13.7% year over year, but earnings declined as lower noninterest income and higher expenses outweighed reduced credit-loss provisioning. The noninterest income comparison reflected a prior-year property valuation write-up and a current-quarter write-down.
² Reported as “Net Income”. ³ Reported as “Earnings per share - diluted”.
: Increased 42 basis points to 3.64%, driven by higher loan volume and yield, lower deposit rates and reduced average FHLB advances.
: Average loan balances rose $19.7 million, or 6.6%, to $316.0 million; loan yield increased 51 basis points to 6.36%.
: Fell to $36,000 from $487,000; the prior-year provision was elevated by a charge-off following foreclosure of a multifamily property.
: Deposits increased $31.1 million, or 9.5%, from December 31, 2025, while core deposits rose $26.2 million, or 13.5%.
